summary: Downscale a video to a target height, preserving aspect, and re-encode at a named profile.

parity.note: Deterministic for a fixed ffmpeg build: libx264 at a pinned preset/crf over identical input bytes emits identical output bytes. The condition is the BUILD, not the box — local and pod run the same pinned ffmpeg, and tests/test_op_media_scale.py asserts the argv is a pure function of params so a drift shows as an argv diff rather than as mystery-different pixels. Across ffmpeg majors this degrades to perceptual; that is a version-pin problem and belongs to the image, not to this op.

height.description: Target height in pixels. Width follows from the source aspect (-2 = nearest even). The DECISION is 'how big'; how it is scaled is the handler's.

height_mode.description: How `height` meets the source. `exact` scales to it in either direction — today's behaviour, the default, and byte-for-byte the argv a chain built by an older engine has always produced. `at_most` clamps to min(height, source height): the pod already holds the file open, so 'do not upscale' is decided where the number lives instead of costing the caller one header probe per candidate — ~50 of them on a real palette, and on a box that may hold no media not a probe it can make at all. GEOMETRY either way, and still the caller's `height`: nothing here says which tier chose it. Same polarity as `tonemap: auto` and as media.filmstrip measuring duration instead of being told it.

encode_profile.description: Named quality tier, NOT encoder flags. `-preset veryfast -crf 26` is tuning and stays in the handler (scripts/render_profile.py is the same SSOT pattern). Sending argv here would publish the encoder ladder and void additionalProperties:false.

seek.description: Start this many seconds into the source. GEOMETRY on the source's own axis, the same class of fact as `height` — nothing here says which beat chose it or why. Absent (or 0) = from the start, byte-for-byte the pre-window argv. Without it a cutaway proxy encodes the WHOLE master: measured 10.1 s per ref against ~4 s for the window that is actually played.

duration.description: Encode only this many seconds from `seek`. Geometry, paired with `seek`; absent = to the end.

fps.description: Resample to this constant frame rate. Stock lands at 23.976 or 25 and a player left to retime it live JUDDERS. Same spelling and same range as media.normalize.fps — one vocabulary. Absent = the source's own rate, unchanged.

tonemap.description: Source HDR transfer to tonemap SDR→bt709. The enum and the zscale+tonemap=hable chain are media.normalize's, imported rather than respelled, so ingest and a preview cannot disagree about what HLG becomes. `auto` MEASURES the source's transfer in the handler — the only place the file exists on the pod contour, and the same polarity as media.filmstrip measuring duration instead of being told it. Without this an HLG stock cutaway previews washed out.
